Figure_R5_regions_heads.description: Area-weighted median D (dB; dense OPM array vs Neuromag (306 channels), sensor plus brain noise, 10-nAm cortical-normal dipoles; medial wall excluded) per lobe from g3b_summary.json placement_D['<anatomy>/<placement>/combined/intrinsic+brain'].by_lobe, placement 'top' in (a) and 'counterfactual_x-centred' in (b). The parcel rows of (a) are computed here from g3b_targets_<anatomy>.csv: D = 20 log10(detect_opm_dense_opm_intrinsic+brain / detect_squid_top_combined_intrinsic+brain) per target, targets with region '*unknown' (medial wall) left out, both hemispheres pooled, area-weighted median with weights area_mm2 (opmsquid.pediatric.weighted_median: values sorted, the first reaching half the cumulative area); the same rule on the same files reproduces the stored lobe medians to within 4.7e-04 dB (CSV rounding). Mesial temporal = parahippocampal + entorhinal. The target files hold no detectability for the laterally centred scaled helmet (squid:counterfactual_x-centred), so (b) has lobes only. Diverging colour scale centred at 0 dB, symmetric (+/-3.5 dB), shared by both panels. Heads ordered by class (adult; scaled adult, size only; infant template; individual child), then head circumference, largest first: Adult 58.6 cm, School size 52.5 cm, 2-y size 49.5 cm, 24 mo 49.5 cm, 18 mo 49.1 cm, 12 mo 46.9 cm, Child C 53.5 cm, Child A 52.0 cm, Child B 48.6 cm.
Figure_R5_regions_heads.alt: Two heat maps of D in decibels: rows are six lobes and four temporal or precentral parcel groups, columns the nine heads grouped by class and ordered by head circumference (46.9-58.6 cm). Every cell is positive (+0.17 to +3.06 dB), so the dense OPM array is ahead of Neuromag in every region of every head. In the fixed adult helmet 72 of 80 cells of the smaller heads exceed the adult's value in the same row; in the helmet scaled with the head 39 of 48 lobe cells are at or below it. The parcel rows of the second map are hatched as not stored.
Figure_R5_regions_heads.caption_draft: Figure R5. Which brain regions favour the OPM at which head size. Area-weighted median D, dense OPM array minus Neuromag (306 channels), sensor plus brain noise, by lobe and for precentral, superior temporal, parahippocampal and mesial temporal (parahippocampal + entorhinal) cortex, both hemispheres, medial wall excluded; right: cortical targets per cell (range over the heads). (a) The fixed adult helmet at top contact. (b) The helmet scaled with the head, laterally centred (lobes only: parcel values were not stored for this helmet). Head circumference 46.9-58.6 cm; the infant heads are average templates, the children individual MRIs.

Figure_R6_pediatric_D.description: g3b_summary.json comparisons['<anatomy>/opm_dense/combined/<condition>/detect'] for condition 'intrinsic+brain' (filled) and 'projected' (open): d_child.median with ci95 in (a), delta.median with ci95 in (b). The adult's D is d_adult.median, identical in every comparison (checked): +1.00 dB (sensor plus brain noise), +0.86 dB (after the 8-term projection). Intervals: parcel bootstrap, 95 %, 1,000 resamples. Delta is vertex-wise for the scaled copies (the same cortical vertex; 6,855-6,949 homologous targets) and the area-weighted median of parcel differences for the templates and children (no vertex correspondence; 65-66 Desikan-Killiany parcels). Heads ordered by class (adult; scaled adult, size only; infant template; individual child), then head circumference, largest first: Adult 58.6 cm, School size 52.5 cm, 2-y size 49.5 cm, 24 mo 49.5 cm, 18 mo 49.1 cm, 12 mo 46.9 cm, Child C 53.5 cm, Child A 52.0 cm, Child B 48.6 cm.
Figure_R6_pediatric_D.alt: Two dot plots with one row per smaller head: left, each head's D with vertical lines at the adult's D; right, Delta with 95 % intervals, each class labelled with its estimator. With sensor plus brain noise Delta is positive in 8 of 8 heads, with the interval above zero in 7 (not: Child C); after the projection the interval includes zero for Child C, Child A.
Figure_R6_pediatric_D.caption_draft: Figure R6. Smaller heads in the fixed adult helmet. (a) D_head, dense OPM array minus Neuromag (306 channels), at top contact; vertical lines: the adult's D (solid: sensor plus brain noise; dashed: the room field added and removed by the 8-term projection). (b) Delta = D_head - D_adult, vertex-wise for the scaled adults and parcel-matched for the templates and children (labelled in the panel). Filled: sensor plus brain noise; open: after the 8-term projection. Lines: 95 % parcel-bootstrap intervals (spatial, within one anatomy; no between-subject variability). With sensor plus brain noise Delta is +0.17 to +1.07 dB over the eight heads and +0.17 to +0.41 dB for the individual children.

Figure_R7_helmet_fit.description: (a) g3b_summary.json placement_D['<anatomy>/<placement>/combined/intrinsic+brain'].median for centred, top, x-centred, counterfactual and counterfactual_x-centred; dashed: the adult at top (+1.00 dB) and counterfactual_x-centred (+1.28 dB); grey band: the adult over its 12 source-blind placements in the fixed helmet (top, back and the ten +-5 mm x/y, pitch +-10, roll +-5 and yaw +-10 deg variants; docs/methods.md), +0.98 to +1.43 dB. (b) sensor_distances['<anatomy>']['squid:top' | 'squid:counterfactual_x-centred'].median_mm (median magnetometer coil-to-scalp distance); dotted: the sphere model's 18 mm (g3a_size_benchmark.json size_following[*].xi_squid_mm; Jas et al. 2026, docs/literature/jas2026.md section 2.1). (c) comparisons['<anatomy>/<array>/combined/<condition>/detect'].d_child.share_positive (adult: d_adult.share_positive, identical in every comparison), matched array solid, dense array faint; filled sensor plus brain noise, open after the projection. (d) channel_count_control['<anatomy>/combined'].n_sites (numbers) and .d_adult_subsampled.median (the adult's dense array subsampled by farthest-point sampling to that count; same placement and noise) against the adult's full array (dashed). Heads ordered by class (adult; scaled adult, size only; infant template; individual child), then head circumference, largest first: Adult 58.6 cm, School size 52.5 cm, 2-y size 49.5 cm, 24 mo 49.5 cm, 18 mo 49.1 cm, 12 mo 46.9 cm, Child C 53.5 cm, Child A 52.0 cm, Child B 48.6 cm.
Figure_R7_helmet_fit.alt: Four panels. (a) D of nine heads at five helmet conditions: in the fixed helmet the smaller heads' D is +2.07 to +3.65 dB at the adult's pose and +1.19 to +2.13 dB at top contact; in the scaled, laterally centred helmet +0.62 to +1.33 dB, above the adult's +1.28 dB for Child C only. (b) The Neuromag gap at top contact is wider than the adult's for 8 of 8 smaller heads; in the scaled helmet it is narrower than the adult's except for Child C; every gap exceeds the sphere model's 18 mm. (c) The dense array's share of cortex with the OPM ahead is 0.90-1.00 with sensor plus brain noise; the site-matched array's is higher than the adult's in 8 of 8 smaller heads under both conditions. (d) The adult's D falls by 0.27-0.53 dB when its 208-site array is cut to 144-174 sites.
Figure_R7_helmet_fit.caption_draft: Figure R7. Helmet fit and head size, each panel against one fixed reference. (a) D (dense OPM array minus Neuromag (306 channels), sensor plus brain noise) at five helmet conditions; dashed: the adult at top contact and in its own scaled, laterally centred helmet; grey: the adult over its 12 standard placements. (b) Median Neuromag coil-to-scalp gap: 32.6-40.4 mm at top contact (adult 28.4), 25.1-33.1 mm in the scaled, laterally centred helmet (adult 29.6); dotted: the 18-mm gap the sphere model keeps for every head size. (c) Share of cortical area with D > 0 (the preprint's metric), site-matched array (solid) and dense array (faint). (d) Dense OPM sites per head (144-174; adult 208) and the adult's D with its array subsampled to each count. The helmet scaled with the head is an array construction (coil centres scaled), not a device.

Figure_R8_depth_matched.description: g3b_summary.json comparisons['<anatomy>/opm_dense/combined/intrinsic+brain/detect'].delta_by_depth: per depth stratum (lo-hi below the scalp, each head's own depth), the area-weighted median D of the head's cortical targets minus the adult's (delta), with a 95 % interval from resampling parcels in each anatomy (ci95; drawn for the individual children only). Strata with fewer than 10 targets in either head have no delta and are skipped (0-10 mm: the adult has none). Targets per stratum: 15-1,788 (smaller heads), 26-1,572 (adult). Points at stratum centres (60-90 mm at 75 mm); the children's points are offset by 0.7 mm to keep the intervals apart.
Figure_R8_depth_matched.alt: Two line plots of Delta against depth below the scalp. Scaled adults and infant templates: Delta is positive in every stratum. Individual children: Delta is −0.36 to +0.08 dB in the strata shallower than 30 mm, with the interval entirely below zero at 20-25 mm for Child C, Child A, Child B, and positive from 30 mm deeper.
Figure_R8_depth_matched.caption_draft: Figure R8. Depth-matched comparison with the adult. Delta per depth stratum (dense OPM array vs Neuromag (306 channels), sensor plus brain noise, top contact): the area-weighted median D of a head's cortical targets in the stratum minus the adult's in the same stratum (a difference of the two heads' medians). (a) Scaled adults and infant templates. (b) Individual children with 95 % parcel-bootstrap intervals. Strata with fewer than 10 targets in either head are omitted; targets per stratum 15-1,788 (smaller heads), 26-1,572 (adult).

Figure_R9_noise_floor.description: g3b_summary.json sensitivity_median_D_dB['<anatomy>/opm_asd_<n>fT/<array>/combined/intrinsic+brain'] for the OPM white-noise levels of configs/g2_adult.toml (7, 10, 15, 20, 30 fT/sqrt(Hz)); the 15-fT points are the stored sensitivity keys, checked equal to the primary D_median_dB['<anatomy>/<array>/combined/intrinsic+brain/detect']. Neuromag noise unchanged. Vertical lines: the primary level and about 30 fT/sqrt(Hz), the approximate OPM empty-room floor of the Jas et al. (2026) recording (docs/literature/jas2026.md section 5.6: about 28-35 fT/sqrt(Hz), read from the preprint's Fig. 9; a broadband value, not matched to the 1-40 Hz band). Heads ordered by class (adult; scaled adult, size only; infant template; individual child), then head circumference, largest first: Adult 58.6 cm, School size 52.5 cm, 2-y size 49.5 cm, 24 mo 49.5 cm, 18 mo 49.1 cm, 12 mo 46.9 cm, Child C 53.5 cm, Child A 52.0 cm, Child B 48.6 cm.
Figure_R9_noise_floor.alt: Two line plots of D against the OPM white noise, one line per head; every line falls as the noise rises. At 30 fT per root hertz the dense array's D is −0.05 to +0.97 dB (negative for Adult); the site-matched array's is −0.79 to +0.18 dB (negative for 8 of 9 heads).
Figure_R9_noise_floor.caption_draft: Figure R9. The noise condition. D (OPM minus Neuromag (306 channels), sensor plus brain noise, top contact) against the OPM's white sensor noise, Neuromag unchanged. (a) Dense OPM array; (b) site-matched OPM array. Grey line: the primary 15 fT/sqrt(Hz); dotted: about 30 fT/sqrt(Hz), the approximate OPM empty-room floor in the Jas et al. (2026) recording (broadband). At 30 fT/sqrt(Hz) the dense array's D is −0.05 to +0.97 dB (adult −0.05).

Figure_R10_spikes.description: g4_<anatomy>_summary.json paired['<array>/opm_vs_squid/combined/practical@1']['depth<b>'].s50_ratio_squid_over_opm (value, value_bounds, value_censored, ci95) for opm_dense (dark) and opm_matched (light); depth bands from the table header of G4_pediatric_report.md (10-20, 20-30, 30-45, 45-70 mm; every stored location checked to lie in its band). Annotations at 10-20 mm: locations_favouring_opm : locations_favouring_squid, and location_sign_flip_p Holm-adjusted (step-down) over the nine anatomies, computed here for each array separately; the stored p values are uncorrected, and the 10-20 mm band was taken as the single endpoint after seeing the data (post hoc). An open interval end (bootstrap resamples outside the tested 10-320 nAm) is an arrow to the axis edge, an interval open at both ends a dotted line; a censored point estimate (value_bounds) an open marker with a dashed arrow; 'neither reaches 50 %': no estimate. The deeper panel shows all three deeper bands (depth1-depth3). Adult (dagger) at its measured head position (G2), the other heads at top contact. 18 locations per band and anatomy. Heads ordered by class (adult; scaled adult, size only; infant template; individual child), then head circumference, largest first: Adult 58.6 cm, School size 52.5 cm, 2-y size 49.5 cm, 24 mo 49.5 cm, 18 mo 49.1 cm, 12 mo 46.9 cm, Child C 53.5 cm, Child A 52.0 cm, Child B 48.6 cm.
Figure_R10_spikes.alt: Forest plots of the S50 ratio on a log axis with a line at 1. At 10-20 mm the dense array's ratio is 1.18-1.65 in the nine heads, its interval including 1 for Child A; the site-matched array's ratio is 1.05-1.60, its interval including 1 for 5 heads. In the deeper bands the ratios lie near 1 with wide or open intervals; censored or missing estimates: 0, 0 and 8 of 18 at 20-30, 30-45, 45-70 mm.
Figure_R10_spikes.caption_draft: Figure R10. Interictal spikes. Strength for 50 % detection, Neuromag (306 channels) over OPM, paired on identical simulated spikes (practical detector, thresholds frozen at 1 false event per minute); > 1: the OPM detects at a lower strength. Dark: dense OPM; light: site-matched OPM. Lines: 95 % bootstrap intervals over the 18 locations per band; arrows: open ends; open markers: censored estimates. (a) 10-20 mm, dense-array ratios 1.18-1.65; right: locations favouring each system and the location sign-flip p, Holm-adjusted over the nine anatomies (each array separately; dense array largest 0.0225; site-matched array below 0.05 for 2-y size, 18 mo); the endpoint was chosen post hoc. (b) Deeper bands. Dagger: the adult sits at its measured head position, the smaller heads at top contact in the fixed adult helmet.
